trust_decision.summary: Editor-authored page Twig is untrusted and runs in the Twig sandbox; it may read config only through the redacting SandboxConfig facade. The sandbox member gate (GravSecurityPolicy) decides which objects and members it may touch, but PHP-side dump/serialize/cast filters read object state without going through that gate.

landing_point.why: The summary names grav.offsetGet plus a dump filter; print_r is registered here and its implementation is at GravExtension.php:283-286.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The allowlist in security.yaml looks like site-owner configuration, not code, and json_encode belongs to Twig core rather than Grav. Either lets a solver guard only print_r in GravExtension and stop there.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several things must keep working. Trusted theme/plugin templates (unsandboxed) still use print_r/json_encode/yaml_encode on any object. Sandboxed content can still json_encode/print_r a page header (stdClass) and yaml_encode the redacting `config` facade. Removing these filters from the allowlist, or guarding them outside the sandbox, breaks all of that.
